candidates.name: Ischemic Cardiomyopathy
support_spans: High-sensitivity troponin I: 62 ng/mL
Patchy late gadolinium enhancement in multiple walls of the heart
contradict_spans: Cardiac Catheterization:- No significant coronary disease
candidates.why: The elevated troponin and patchy late gadolinium enhancement suggest myocardial damage, but the lack of significant coronary disease on catheterization makes this diagnosis less likely.

candidates.name: Dilated Cardiomyopathy
support_spans: Dilated left ventricular cavity with LV wall hypertrophy
LV ejection fraction: 20-25%
candidates.why: The dilated left ventricle and reduced ejection fraction are characteristic of dilated cardiomyopathy.

candidates.name: Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy
support_spans: LV wall hypertrophy
candidates.why: The presence of LV wall hypertrophy could suggest hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, but the dilated left ventricle is not typical of this condition.

candidates.name: Sarcoidosis
support_spans: PET scan:- Revealed cardiac granulomatous disease
candidates.why: The presence of cardiac granulomatous disease on the PET scan is a strong indicator of sarcoidosis, which can cause heart block, arrhythmias, and heart failure.
candidates.protected_reason: Sarcoidosis is a rare cause of cardiac disease and may be missed if not considered in the differential diagnosis.

candidates.name: Giant Cell Myocarditis
support_spans: Patchy late gadolinium enhancement in multiple walls of the heart
Regional wall motion abnormalities in anterior, septal, and lateral walls
candidates.why: The patchy late gadolinium enhancement and regional wall motion abnormalities on cardiac MRI are consistent with giant cell myocarditis, a rare and potentially fatal disease.
candidates.protected_reason: Giant cell myocarditis is a rare and easily missed diagnosis that requires a high index of suspicion.

candidates.name: Chagas Cardiomyopathy
support_spans: Dilated left ventricular cavity with LV wall hypertrophy
Significant LV desynchrony
candidates.why: The dilated left ventricular cavity with hypertrophy and significant desynchrony are consistent with Chagas cardiomyopathy, a rare cause of heart failure in the United States.
candidates.protected_reason: Chagas disease is a rare cause of cardiomyopathy in non-endemic areas and may be missed if not considered in the differential diagnosis.
